commentary_segments.text: The amplifier does not need to be a full operational amplifier, with lots of gain. A simple transistor amplifier can do it as well. Here the opamp is replaced by a single-stage amplifier followed by a source follower. The open-loop gain is simply the gain of that input transistor as a source follower provides a gain of unity only. This is also the loop gain as easily seen. We can still break the loop where we want. The output resistance is a bit higher now, i.e. 1/g , which is still a lot smaller than R . m2 F The closed-loop gain is usually the easiest one to calculate. It is still R as for the first feedback F amplifier and it is still a transresistance amplifier. In other words, it converts an input current into an output voltage with high accuracy, here with value R . F
